# Pharmlabs

> Open-source pharmaceutical compounding education resource providing hands-on lab exercises for pharmacy students on dosage form preparation, formulation science, and USP standards.

Pharmlabs is a comprehensive educational platform developed at the University of North Carolina that supports pharmacy education through interactive lab exercises covering the full spectrum of pharmaceutical compounding techniques. The resource aligns with American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy standards and emphasizes practical competency in extemporaneous preparation and sterile compounding.

## Core & Sterile Compounding

- [Pharmlabs Homepage](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu): UNC Pharmlabs homepage: open-source pharmaceutical compounding education resource
- [Aseptic Techniques](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/sterile/atech): Lab exercise on aseptic techniques and USP <797> sterile compounding standards
- [Accuracy in Measurement](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/measurementaccuracy): Lab exercise on measurement accuracy, systems, and balance techniques
- [Prescriptions & Medication Orders](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/rxmedorders): Lab exercise on prescription interpretation and extemporaneous preparation

## Liquid Dosage Forms

- [Pharmaceutical Solutions I: Simple, Saturated, Syrups](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/pharmsol1): Lab exercise on simple, saturated, and syrup pharmaceutical solutions
- [Pharmaceutical Solutions II: Nonaqueous Solutions](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/pharmsol2): Lab exercise on nonaqueous solutions, elixirs, and hydroalcoholic formulations
- [Emulsions: Preparation & Stabilization](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/emulsions): Lab exercise on emulsion preparation, stabilization, and HLB theory
- [Colloidal Dispersions](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/colloidaldispersions): Lab exercise on colloidal dispersions, stability, and particle characterization
- [Aesthetic Considerations of Oral Liquid Dosage Forms](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/acoldf): Lab exercise on palatability, flavor masking, and oral liquid aesthetics

## Topical & Semi-Solid Formulations

- [Ointments: Preparation & Evaluation of Drug Release](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/ointments): Lab exercise on ointment preparation and topical drug release evaluation
- [Gels](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/gels): Lab exercise on gel formulation, gelling agents, and topical drug delivery
- [Suppositories](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/suppositories): Lab exercise on suppository preparation, bases, and rectal/vaginal administration

## Solid & Particulate Dosage Forms

- [Capsules](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/capsules): Lab exercise on hard gelatin capsule compounding and USP testing
- [Powders & Granules](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/powders): Lab exercise on powder and granule compounding, sizing, and formulation
- [Lozenges & Medication Sticks](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/lozenges): Lab exercise on lozenge and medication stick compounding techniques

## Specialized Route Formulations

- [Ophthalmic Preparations](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/ophthalmic): Lab exercise on ophthalmic formulations: buffering, isotonicity, sterility
- [Otic Preparations](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/otics): Lab exercise on otic ear medication preparation and nonaqueous vehicles
- [Intranasal Preparations](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/intranasal): Lab exercise on intranasal dosage forms and nasal drug administration
- [Inhalation Preparations](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/inhalation): Lab exercise on inhalation dosage forms and pulmonary drug delivery devices
- [Aerosols, Foams, & Sprays](https://pharmlabs.unc.edu/labexercises/compounding/aerosols): Lab exercise on aerosol dosage forms, propellants, and drug delivery systems
